results.title: Congress leadership directionless blames institutions for poll defeats Shivraj Chouhan
results.description: New Delhi Oct 12 IANS Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Monday launched a sharp attack on the Congress accusing its top leadership of being completely directionless and asserting that this was the primary reason behind the partys repeated electoral defeats across the countrynbspAddressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi Chouhan said For several years Congress has been continuously attacking constitutional institutions Now it has stooped to a point where putting the blame on constitutional institutions for election defeats has become a patternnbspLosing elections one after another and then taking out protests has become the fate of the Congress The reason for the repeated election defeats is not the Election Commission but the directionless leadership of Congress itself Chouhan said pointing to alleged internal differences in the partys Uttar Pradesh Punjab and Karnataka divisionsThe Union Minister further claimed that the Congress had been politically marginalised in several major states for a considerable period citing Tamil Nadu West Bengal Sikkim Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as examplesnbspExcept for three or four states Congress has been reduced to a junior partner in every other state he saidnbspChouhan also accused the Congress of targeting constitutional institutions for political gainnbspCongress cannot win the country over by attacking constitutional institutions simply for the sake of holding onto power he addednbspIn a further attack Chouhan alleged that the Congress routinely criticised institutions whenever their decisions or actions went against the partys interestsCongress is in such a state that when a court verdict goes against it it attacks the court When it loses an election it attacks the Election Commission When the Army eliminates terrorists it attacks the Army Congress has found it impossible to digest Indias progress and the trust of the countrys 140 crore people That is why I say with great anguish that Congress is now joining hands with forces seeking to divide the country Chouhan said reiterating that the partys top leadership was completely directionlessnbspChouhan also took aim at remarks comparing the Congress to Lord Shivas wedding procession and said Just now they were saying that Congress is like Lord Shivas wedding procession They are talking about Lord Shivas procession while opposing Lord Ram This is not Lord Shivas wedding procession it is a group of troublemakers spreading chaos and trying to create disorder on the streets he saidThe Agriculture Minister also alleged that the Congress and the INDIA bloc were influenced by foreign powers and accused them of associating with groups and individuals whom he described as being opposed to Indias interestsnbspCongress and the INDIA bloc have now become puppets in the hands of foreign powers For the sake of power they sometimes rely on the Left sometimes on cockroaches sometimes on antinational forces like George Soros and sometimes on NGOs he addedReferring to Rahul Gandhis earlier statements Chouhan said Rahul Gandhi had once said that his fight is against the Indian state itself what does this mean Rahul Gandhi This shows how low Congress and Rahul have stoopednbspThe remarks came amid the Congressled INDIA blocs march towards the Supreme Court seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rollsnbspOpposition leaders have alleged irregularities in the revision exercise and raised concerns over the electoral rolls while the BJP has defended the process and accused the Congress of politicising the issueIANS

results.title: Federal Judge Orders Trump to Stop Airing Ads Paid for by Taxpayers
results.description: A federal judge ordered the Trump administration on Sunday to stop airing ads funded by taxpayers that promote President Donald Trump and mirror some of his old campaign ads, effective immediately. The plaintiffs in the case argue that the White House exceeded congressional authorization and violated “restrictions on publicity and propaganda.” NBC’s Garrett Haake reports for TODAY.

results.title: 'Demolition of democracy': Ex-Pakistani Prez on emergency imposition in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
results.description: Islamabad, Oct 12 (IANS) Former Pakistani President Arif Alvi on Monday strongly condemned the federal government's decision to impose emergency and Governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, describing the move as the "demolition of democracy". The statement came after the federal government on Sunday imposed a state of emergency in 12 districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and suspended the provincial government led by jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. In a post on X, Alvi said that the province had been taken over by what he described as an "unrepresentative, fraudulent set-up in Islamabad". He asserted that only the people of KP had the right to remove their government, accusing the "unelected, gun-imposed usurpers in Islamabad" of overriding the people's mandate. Custom Ad: Multiplex "All reports suggest that the only sticking point was a meeting with Mr Imran Khan, the people's falsely incarcerated leader. Those who cannot bear even his image emerging from the dungeons they hold him in are dragging the country down in their petty, spiteful, malicious hatred. Personal animosity is consuming Pakistan. Poverty and elite capture are up. Those who collude spinelessly grow richer, and plotocracy and fascism rise," the former Pakistani President stated. "Never in Pakistan's history have children been seized and beaten to force their parents into submission. Destruction of property is the police's new routine. Elected PTI representatives continue to be tortured and kidnapped by masked regime changers, while the judiciary kneels at the altar of the wicked," he added. Drawing parallels with Balochistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), Alvi said that the brutal suppression of peaceful and constitutional protests over missing persons in Balochistan, along with recent life sentences handed down to Baloch women activists, sent a message that peaceful dissent would not be tolerated. He said that a similar message had been conveyed in PoK, where massive peaceful protests were "viciously strangled", leaving dozens dead. Questioning whether Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was now being sent the same message by the "destroyers of Pakistan" -- the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and their "Gods" -- Alvi warned of a similar fate for the province. Meanwhile, the Sindh High Court Bar Association (SHCBA) and Karachi Bar Association (KBA) have criticised the Pakistani government's decision to impose emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming it "undemocratic" and declaring that the legal fraternity will observe a 'black day' in solidarity with the people. The SCHBA called on authorities to respect the fundamental rights of the people and take measures to restore democracy, Pakistani daily Dawn reported. --IANS scor/sd/
